name: Navigation: Home, Inbox, Search, Browse tile palette, New chat
what: A compact sidebar offers Home (conversations), Inbox with a waiting count, Calendar (stub), Search and Browse, then Create New Chat; Browse opens a two-column tile palette of Projects, Files, Crons, Webhooks, Keychain, Apps, Memory, Skills, Loops and Admin with one-line blurbs.
how: renderSidebarTop() with navRow/actionRow; destinations() builds the palette with permission checks (can('loops'), can('admin')); VIEWS list of 13 views; arrow-key tile navigation.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's six-tab cockpit and QM's resource palette make different bets; QM hides resources behind Browse while chat dominates.
notes: SPEC's Wall of Shame criticises each artifact page having its own design instead of one group-by backbone.

name: Scope-centred Projects page
what: One page per scope shows its conversations, its files, webhooks, crons, apps and skills with manage actions, and a settings column for members, Slack link, model, pinned channel header and ambient policy. The list groups Personal, Web and Slack scopes with counts and last activity.
how: gridTpl() groups contexts by kind; detailTpl() renders panels and aside (projectMembersSection, projectSlackSection, contextModelSection, channelHeaderSection, ambientPolicySection); loadScopeResources fetches /api/scope-resources; empty state says the project is ready for work.
verevonRelevance: This is the 'one view of the room's computer and resources' the Verevon plan calls a QM lead (S1.6/S4.5); it is the closest reference for a Space home tab layout.
notes: No full-page Space home beyond this page; 'Projects' and 'Contexts' are used interchangeably in code.

name: Session top bar shows the scope's tools with live counts
what: Inside a conversation the top bar shows a breadcrumb to the project plus tool buttons for Crons, Files, Memory, Apps, Skills and Keychain scoped to that conversation's scope, with cached counts of enabled crons and live apps; opening a tool keeps the session context.
how: sessionTopbarTpl(); TOOL_COUNTERS caches counts for 60 s per scope; setScopedSession() carries scope into crons/files/memory views; parent and fork badges link back.
verevonRelevance: Makes the agent's context legible at the point of conversation; a good pattern for Space chat headers.

name: Sidebar organisation: pinned, recent by project, archive, colours, multi-select
what: Conversations are split into Pinned and Recent, with project/channel groups holding their sessions, an Archived toggle, status filter (active, waiting, archived), per-conversation colours and emoji status, awaiting/working marks, read-only locks for non-continuable sessions, shift-click range selection with bulk actions, and a 'Web only' filter.
how: splitPinned(), recentProjectSeeds() and ChatBrowseStatus in session-list.ts; session rows in sessions.ts carry colour via --session-color, status marks, share/archive/pin actions; selection state machine in session-select.ts; setWebOnly().
verevonRelevance: Sidebar organisation is a gap in Verevon (no cross-room aggregates); this is a complete reference including bulk selection.

name: Composer design: pickers, paste chips and runtime inheritance
what: The composer combines a model/effort/fast-mode picker with up to eight saved presets, long pastes that become viewable and editable chips, drag/drop and folder drop, emoji and slash completion, and an upgrade banner when the org's recommended runtime moves ahead of the scope's pinned runtime (Upgrade, Keep mine, Inherit future defaults).
how: composer-loadout LOADOUT_CAP 8 with upsert/reconcile; pasteChipLabel and a paste dialog with 'Insert into message'; SLASH_TOKEN; upgradeAvailable banner calling changeScopeRuntime({harnessId,modelId}|{keep:true}|{inherit:true}); effort levels low..ultracode, adaptive and provider default.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's room composer is a plain streamChat box; model presets and paste chips are cheap wins once Spaces allow model choice.

name: Transcript reading: collapsed prompts, completed-work disclosure, paged history
what: Long latest prompts start as a two-line preview with Show more, finished tool work collapses into one timed disclosure while the answer stays visible, history loads by turns (older pages can load during live turns), scrolled-up readers are not yanked, and every message has a permalink.
how: QA doc records the before and after; transcript-viewport.ts and timeline.ts; TAIL_TURNS paging; messageEntrySeqs() map messages to entry seqs for links.
verevonRelevance: Reading ergonomics for long agent threads in a shared room; informs Verevon's tool-call card design.

name: Multiview with up to 16 tiled panes and responsive density
what: People can tile up to 16 conversations or views side by side by dragging sidebar rows to pane edges; each pane picks a density tier from its size, restores on reload, syncs across devices, and shows a compact header in the desktop app.
how: dockview-core layout with split-layout.ts limits MAX_TILES/MAX_PANES 16, pane-kinds for drag payloads, serializedTileCount guard, remote split sync, density.ts per-pane tier.
verevonRelevance: Watching several rooms and agent runs at once is a power-user feature neither Teams nor Slack offers; consider for Verevon's Work cockpit.

name: Empty states and suggested starters
what: The empty personal chat shows up to three suggested activities (generated per person or from operator JSON) that fill an editable draft instead of sending; shared contexts and existing chats do not show them; new projects show a 'ready for work' panel.
how: SuggestedActivity {id,title,prompt,icon}; suggestions fade when a draft or attachment exists and are inert to assistive tech when collapsed; welcome-ideas and cohort welcome copy.
verevonRelevance: Activation pattern for empty Spaces; the 'fill a draft, never send' rule avoids accidental agent runs.
notes: docs/SPEC.md:160 records that YC-specific welcome copy remains in the public app after a scrub (qm#1504); the activity generation prompt also carries a 'yc' icon rule (src/suggestions/activities.ts:11-19).

name: Slack-to-web continuity cues
what: In Slack, a pinned channel header (or DM topic) names the model in use with a link to the scope's web settings, long-running work shows a 'Follow via QM Web' link, cron deliveries link to cron settings, and the web Projects page lists Slack channels and DMs under a 'Slack' group; conversations from Slack open read-only in the web.
how: createSurfaceHeaderEnsurer() sets topic or pins/updates/removes a bot message according to the channel header setting (default off in org config); channelWelcomeMessage on join; sidebar 'Web only' setting hides Slack conversations.
verevonRelevance: A concrete way for an external channel adapter to point back to the canonical Space without duplicating its UI.
notes: Header is skipped for externally shared channels and group DMs.

name: Mixed rooms with external participants (org-wide, off by default)
what: An admin can allow internal members to use the agent in Slack rooms whose audience includes an external user (Slack Connect member or guest). The agent's replies and anything it reads there are visible to those externals, and externals themselves still cannot interact. A separate override list marks trusted Slack users as internal.
how: config-store getExternalSlackParticipants/getInternalMemberOverrides; the Slack turn handler refuses turns whose audience has an external guest unless the org flag is on; Admin Integrations shows two cards with explicit warnings that internal-member access includes organisation credentials in all-internal rooms.
verevonRelevance: Explicit, default-off switch for shared rooms that include outsiders; Verevon's guest/external-channel design (plan S5.1) needs the same 'externals read but cannot act' stance.

name: Slack context is mirror-first with live fallback and honest limits
what: The agent reads conversation context from stored Slack events first, falls back to live history, and says plainly when context may be incomplete; a shared hosted Slack app uses a 15-message history limit and tells the user when Slack rate-limits history reads, offering to set up their own app.
how: createSlackHistoryReader() with MIRROR_CONTEXT_NOTE, liveHistory fallback and expansion failure counters; SHARED_SLACK_HISTORY_LIMIT=15; createSlackRateLimitNotice() posts a DM notice or ephemeral hint once per minute per user.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon channel adapter will hit provider history limits; stating the limitation in-band avoids the agent confidently answering from partial context.

name: Agent plan task list shown in replies
what: The agent's own per-run task list (pending, in progress, completed, skipped, failed) is stored per session and rendered as a section in the Slack reply and delivery, so people see the plan and progress without opening the web UI.
how: TaskStore keyed by sessionId and originRunId with status events; surface tools attach taskList {id,title,status} to deliveries; Slack deliveries render renderTaskList() into a section block; harness adapters bridge their native todo tools.
verevonRelevance: A lightweight, agent-owned task list is the closest QM gets to tasks in a room; Verevon's orchestration todos are per thread and could surface the same way.
notes: These are agent plans, not human task boards; no kanban or boards exist in QM.

name: Other bots can address the agent but never carry human authority
what: Posts from other Slack bots can mention or reach the agent, but they are marked botAuthored/botActor, are not live-human turns and so cannot use a person's keychain or sharing posture; per-bot behaviour is set in the channel's bot ledger.
how: eventIdentity() resolves bot ids via bots.info; dispatch sets botAuthored and omits liveActor for bots; allowActor refuses bots when an allowlist exists; the ambient judge treats ledger modes ignore, rollup, action and user.
verevonRelevance: Bot-to-agent messaging is a realistic Space scenario (CI bots, alerting); the rule 'bots can ask, only people can authorise' is a clean boundary.

name: Acting as a person means drafting, not sending
what: Skills create drafts in the person's own Slack composer (through their per-user OAuth) or Gmail drafts written from a learned voice profile; nothing is sent and the agent cannot list, edit or delete drafts afterwards, so the person always sends.
how: slack-drafts skill uses the person's Slack user token on the sandbox ($VAULT_TOKEN_SLACK_COM) through a bundled helper; email-voice-profile builds voice/email-voice-profile.md and email-draft-in-voice requires reading the full thread and a self-check; authority stays with the human sender.
verevonRelevance: A strong pattern for 'agent works like a human' without impersonation: prepare in the person's own client, never post in their name.
notes: Live Slack scenario 'mu-authority-not-on-behalf-of-others' pins the refusal to send on another person's behalf.

name: Agent can list, read, message, start and fork sidebar conversations
what: On web turns the agent can list the sessions people see in their sidebar for this context, read their transcripts, send a private note to another session without starting a turn, start a clean new session, or fork the current one; new and forked sessions appear under the person's name and are refused on automated turns.
how: sessions tool actions list/search/read/send_message/new/fork; list and read are scoped to the current context and viewer; messages arrive as internal context, not as a person's request; creation requires a person attending the turn.
verevonRelevance: Lets a room agent split a topic into its own thread at a human's request, comparable to Teams/Slack thread-from-message but agent-initiated.

name: Each Slack thread is its own session inside a shared scope
what: A channel is one scope (shared memory, files, computer) but every Slack thread, and every DM thread, is a separate conversation with its own transcript, so context stays tight per thread while resources are shared per room. A plain DM is one session per DM channel.
how: thread refs are dm:<channel>[:<ts>], ch:<channel>:<root> and grp:<channel>:<root>; slackThreadRefCandidates() resolves which session a message belongs to; Session {scopeId, threadRef}; external-access accounts prefix refs with slack-account:<team>:.
verevonRelevance: Clarifies the thread-versus-room split Verevon needs: threads are conversations, the Space owns the resources and instructions they share.

name: Scheduled send through one-shot or recurring verbatim relays
what: A person can ask the agent to send an exact message later or on a schedule to themselves, a teammate, a channel or a group DM; one-shot times (firstFireAt) auto-cancel after firing, and a message addressed to someone other than the owner carries an attribution footer and needs that recipient's consent when it is a standing delivery.
how: cron tool with text (verbatim) instead of task, destination via recipient/channel/participants; runTrigger() takes the message branch (status ok) and calls reachEnqueue with attributeAs=<owner display name>; consent notice asks the recipient to accept or decline.
verevonRelevance: Scheduled send is absent in Verevon rooms; reusing cron machinery for message relays (with attribution and consent) avoids a separate feature.
notes: No user-facing 'schedule send' button in the web composer; it is agent-mediated.

name: Several Slack accounts and workspaces per deployment
what: One deployment can run multiple Slack apps or workspaces (including a partner workspace), each with its own tokens and events mode; deliveries and thread refs carry the account and team so replies go back through the right client.
how: SLACK_ACCOUNTS JSON array validated for ids and tokens per mode; clientForAccount(accountId, teamId) routes deliveries; Destination.slackAccountId/slackTeamId/slackPolicyNamespace; Socket Mode or HTTP Events per account.
verevonRelevance: Multi-workspace channel adapters (Slack workspaces, Teams tenants) need account-scoped identity on every destination; this is a working shape.

name: Agent can add custom emoji to the Slack workspace
what: The agent can upload a custom Slack emoji (PNG or GIF) on the person's behalf using their own Slack web session or a configured fallback, then use it in reactions and replies.
how: POST /v1/emoji requires an agent capability token; runEmojiUpload validates the emoji name and workspace URL (only https *.slack.com) and drives the browser-session uploader; the ack-emoji picker later samples the workspace's custom emoji.
verevonRelevance: A niche personalization feature; the point for Verevon is that surface-specific admin actions can live behind the same capability-token API instead of in the core model.
notes: Relies on a browser-session path, not an official API.

name: Instruction hierarchy: org SOUL, scope instructions and channel guidance with history
what: Agent behaviour is layered: organisation instructions ('SOUL') take precedence over the scope's instructions, and the agent itself can read and edit its standing 'guidance' for the current channel or conversation (edit one exact passage or replace all). Admins edit the org SOUL with a saved revision, a current draft and a version history.
how: composeSoul() puts org instructions first and labels scope instructions as subordinate; config-store setSoulIfVersion() is a compare-and-swap on a version number; the guidance tool has scope channel|conversation, actions edit/replace and fails unless the old passage appears exactly once; org-wide policy is always layered above and cannot be overridden by guidance.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon's authored-instruction hierarchy (platform, org, Space, persona); QM adds agent-editable room guidance with exact-passage edits and CAS versions, while SECURITY.md concedes edits are not uniformly bounded by an org floor or human approval.
notes: SECURITY.md lists unversioned or unbounded standing-instruction edits as a known governance gap.
